actual_scope: Prove and independently verify the sharp sup-norm rounding error for two distinct normalized real Walsh axes with one intervening integer grid shear on four coordinates, for every directed shear and every integer coefficient.
scope_change_reason: The donor assigned seed 83 to independent verification/formalization. Among three narrow candidates, seed 83 modulo 3 selected the explicit unclaimed interleaved-shear question in PR6140. This is a written scoped theorem and independent exact implementation, not a proof-assistant formalization or a completed selected-caller interface proof. The original card is retained verbatim for provenance.
bottleneck_link: Precision side result: establishes when a pure-Walsh rounding guarantee cannot be carried across an exact grid-preserving gate. It may inform a later precision_tape caller audit, but does not discharge that assumption or improve a paid supplier profile.
stop_rule: One experiment only: all 12 distinct ordered coordinate pairs, two distinct Walsh axes, one integer coefficient. Stop after a universal upper proof, fixed-source affine witnesses for both coefficient signs, complete mod-8 input and mod-4 coefficient census, and independent negative controls. Do not expand to more stages or multiple shears.
evidence: PROOF.md proves sharp error h*(abs(m)+3)/4 for every integer m; WITNESSES.json supplies 24 fixed inputs. RESULT.json records independent complete-vector comparisons on 196608 residue cases, 768 large signed cases, 2916 reverse-axis cases, and 16 rejected controls. This is a scoped mathematical proof with finite corroboration, not formal verification of the multiplication theorem.
